_comment: Phase 4. A provider's rolling P99 has broken its latency contract.
THE THRESHOLD IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN
1000ms, against an observed healthy P99 of 150ms for mockpsp:authorize.
That is ~6.7x headroom, which is deliberate: this alert exists to catch a
provider degrading, not to report normal variance, and an alert that cries
wolf during a clean run gets muted and then ignored - at which point it is
worse than absent, because the dashboard still shows it as configured.
WHY THIS SERIES AND NOT http.client.requests
payorch.provider.latency.p99 comes from RollingLatency, which merges
histogram buckets across a sliding window. It is the same number phase 5
routes on. Alerting on a different one would mean the alert and the router
could disagree about which provider is slow, and the router would win
-1 means 'no calls in the window', which is not a breach and not a zero.
It is below the threshold so it cannot fire, which is the correct
behaviour and the reason the gauge returns -1 rather than 0.

annotations.description: Rolling P99 for {{$labels.psp}}:{{$labels.operation}} exceeded 1000ms (healthy is ~150ms). This is the same number phase 5 routes on, so routing decisions are being made against a degraded provider.
